RISK-01 (graph-native-brain): ArcadeDB high availability is young (Raft only since v26.4.1), and with no bake-off (D-GNB-22) its gates are proved only once P3 and P4 are under way
RISK-02 (graph-native-brain): A small team owns a database fork
RISK-03 (graph-native-brain): The migration loses or corrupts data
RISK-04 (graph-native-brain): ACL semantics drift between Python and the engine
RISK-05 (graph-native-brain): Upstream relicensing
RISK-06 (graph-native-brain): (Extended implementation, E1) Cost of 3 memory-heavy cloudscale servers, one per physical host
RISK-07 (graph-native-brain): Hot-path latency for `/secured/query` scope expansion and overlay reads
RISK-08 (graph-native-brain): Cluster-first and other brain work land new tables mid-migration
RISK-09 (graph-native-brain): The geometry thesis fails
RISK-10 (graph-native-brain): PostgreSQL control tables become critical while PostgreSQL HA is off
RISK-11 (graph-native-brain): The validity check and subclass matching slow every read
RISK-12 (graph-native-brain): The ontology grows into a modelling project tenants can't maintain
RISK-13 (graph-native-brain): Profile caches grow with the number of tenants
RISK-14 (graph-native-brain): The SeDM folder and the app build drift apart
RISK-15 (graph-native-brain): A tenant marks a high-fan-out relation (many edges per node) transitive or symmetric and slows its own walks
RISK-16 (graph-native-brain): OpenBao stays sealed after a restart (no HSM): new pods, volume unlocks and DEK unwraps wait for operators

RISK-17 (graph-native-brain): The IPsec link is a single point of failure for the brain's read path until a second tunnel endpoint exists. Since ADR-0009 (develop, tenant data plane on cloudscale) the brain's read path stays inside cloudscale, and the link is that single point for every relayed `/secured/` request and the AKS-si
RISK-18 (graph-native-brain): The brain shares its Kubernetes control plane with the GPU nodes that run the LLM over untrusted documents
RISK-19 (graph-native-brain): All brain compute runs in one cloudscale region (LPG); losing it means restoring every tenant into a cluster rebuilt in RMA

RISK-20 (graph-native-brain): The strict chain (§11.1) lengthens the calendar: the waves pass each cut-over stage in turn (P8 flips only once every wave reads from the graph), P10–P12 follow P9 instead of filling the cut-over soaks, and 24 owner checkpoints are waits
RISK-21 (graph-native-brain): Overlap (D-GNB-25) splits the team's attention: features are built while tenants move through the cut-over
RISK-22 (graph-native-brain): In the basis the engine and an unsealed OpenBao share the CPU node with production Weaviate, the k3s server and the strongSwan endpoint (D-GNB-27)

RISK-23 (graph-native-brain): In the basis there is no failover: an engine, OpenBao or node failure stops the brain routes until a restart or restore; from `graph_primary` on they answer 503 meanwhile

RISK-24 (graph-native-brain): No independent security review of the isolation plugins in the basis; one person signs architecture and security, and as sole code owner merges their own pull requests by admin bypass
